get.summary: Realtime Server-Sent-Events stream of a session's tracking events
get.description: A standards-based, one-directional server-to-client SSE stream. Accepts `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` or, since browsers' native `EventSource` cannot set custom headers, a `?access_token=<jwt>` query parameter fallback. Emits `data:` frames of TrackingEvent JSON as they occur, periodic `event: ping` heartbeats, and a final `event: closed` frame once the session completes.

parameters.name: access_token
parameters.description: JWT access token, used when an Authorization header cannot be set (e.g. browser EventSource).

get.summary: This organization's real API request/latency/error analytics
get.description: Aggregated from the real per-request `ApiRequestLog` table (see /docs on request logging) — not estimated or sampled for the headline totals. Per-row breakdowns (top endpoints, device mix, requests/minute) are computed over a bounded recent sample for very high-traffic orgs; `data.sampled` is `true` when that cap was hit.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days back to aggregate (1-90, default 7)

get.summary: Look up an OAuth2 client's display name and grantable scopes (public, unauthenticated)
get.description: Called by the real consent page (src/app/oauth/authorize/page.tsx) before the user is even asked to approve anything, so it can show "App X wants access to...". No secrets are exposed here.

200.description: The client's display name and which of the requested scopes it's actually registered for

post.summary: Record the logged-in user's consent decision (approve/deny)
post.description: Requires the approving user's own Bearer token. Granted scopes are the real intersection of what the client is registered for AND what the approving user's own role scopes allow — a user can never consent to handing out permissions they don't have themselves.

200.description: Where to redirect the browser next (with `code`+`state`, or `error=access_denied`)

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code (with PKCE) or refresh token for real access/refresh tokens
post.description: No Bearer/API-key auth on this route itself — the caller authenticates via `client_id`/`client_secret` (authorization_code grant) or the refresh token itself (refresh_token grant), the standard OAuth2 token-endpoint pattern (RFC 6749).

200.description: A real access/refresh token pair, scoped to what the user actually consented to

get.summary: Real security posture for the caller's org — inactive, expired, near-expiration, compromised keys, and failed-auth spikes
get.description: Every section here is a genuine query against real tables, not a mocked dashboard. `compromisedKeys` is honestly manual-flag-only (the `revokedReason` set on revoke) — this app has no external leaked-key-scanning service, so it never fabricates a 'detected' result. `failedAuthSpikes` is derived from real `ApiRequestLog` 401 rows in the last 24h, grouped by API key.

get.summary: List every real organization on the platform
get.description: Requires a Bearer-token principal with `User.isPlatformAdmin = true` — gated by `requirePlatformAdmin()`, not a scope, since this is orthogonal to in-org roles/scopes. API-key principals can never satisfy this, by construction (see `resolvePrincipal`).

200.description: Paginated list of every real organization

get.summary: List every real API key across every organization
get.description: Real cross-org data, each key annotated with its real owning organization's name/slug. Supports `?orgId=` to narrow to one org. Same `requirePlatformAdmin()` gate as `/platform/organizations`.

200.description: Paginated cross-org list of real API keys (secrets never included)

delete.description: The one mutation exposed to platform admins — revocation only (not rotation, which stays a per-tenant self-service action). Writes a real audit event under the key's own org with `metadata.viaPlatformAdmin: true`, and notifies the key's real owner if it has one.
